title: Delete in Edit Library Part is enabled only after the page is reloaded
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test at the test location only, on no work order and with no open return, credit or part request, so it can be deleted later in the test.
  • Use a desktop browser that can open a second tab on the same ShopView address, signed in as the same user.
  • Start in browser tab 1 on the Part Library page (Parts in the top bar, then Part Library in the left menu).
custom_steps:
1. In tab 1, type part A's part number in the Search box.
  2. In tab 1, click the part A row.
  3. In tab 1, click the pencil icon beside the entry's name in the Part details panel.
  4. Open a second browser tab on the same ShopView address.
  5. In tab 2, click Parts in the top bar.
  6. In tab 2, click Inventory in the left menu.
  7. In tab 2, type part A's part number in the Search box.
  8. In tab 2, click the part A row.
  9. In tab 2, click Delete Part.
  10. Switch back to tab 1 without reloading it.
  11. In tab 1, hover over the Delete button at the bottom left of the window.
  12. In tab 1, click Cancel.
  13. In tab 1, click the pencil icon beside the entry's name.
  14. In tab 1, click Cancel again.
  15. In tab 1, reload the page.
  16. In tab 1, click the pencil icon beside the entry's name once more.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part A's entry is listed.

Step 2:

  • The entry's detail page opens and shows "Total parts" 1.

Step 3:

  • The "Edit Library Part" window opens, and its Delete button, bottom left, is dimmed (disabled) because part A uses the entry.

Step 4:

  • A second tab opens.

Step 5:

  • Tab 2 shows the Parts left menu.

Step 6:

  • Tab 2 shows the Inventory page.

Step 7:

  • Part A is listed in tab 2.

Step 8:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 9:

  • The window closes in tab 2 and part A leaves the list: it is deleted.

Step 10:

  • Tab 1 still shows the Edit Library Part window: it was not reloaded.

Step 11:

  • The Delete button is still dimmed, and hovering it shows "Part cannot be deleted. Please delete related parts first.": it shows the entry as it was when the page opened.

Step 12:

  • The window closes.

Step 13:

  • The window opens again and its Delete button is still dimmed: closing and opening the window does not update it.

Step 14:

  • The window closes.

Step 15:

  • The detail page reloads and now shows "Total parts" 0.

Step 16:

  • The "Edit Library Part" window opens and its Delete button is now enabled.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 35 (edited 27 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10824 (Story 11, The Part Library Is Browse and Edit Only)

  • S11-E5: “The Delete button in the "Edit Library Part" window reflects the entry as it was when its detail page opened. If the last part, part request or part return using the entry goes away elsewhere, Delete becomes enabled after the page is reloaded.”
  • S11-R3c: “While an inventory part, an open part request or a part return still uses the entry, the Delete button is disabled and hovering it shows "Part cannot be deleted. Please delete related parts first."”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Delete on a Part Library entry a part still uses | "Part cannot be deleted. Please delete related parts first." | Hover text on the disabled Delete button (S11-R3c)”

From: Product's answers to questions 13 to 27 (Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, Google Doc https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pkAPGqWVTdtYorNN4SVNl9HkHxuuB9czro_y2DbUeEM/edit, saved word for word in full-pass-2026-10-27/ANSWERS-13-27-2026-10-27.md), read 28 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, answer 15: “No. Delete stays disabled until the page is reloaded (S11-E5). Note that an open part request or a part return using the entry also keeps Delete disabled, not only an inventory part (S11-R3c).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Parts Lifecycle Update" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE), 13 Oct 2026 copy, unchanged when re-read on 27 Oct 2026: board "7.2 An entry opens its detail page". Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the quotes above.

The board 7.2 note quoted below says the entry "can be edited and deleted" on its page. Product confirmed on 27 Oct 2026 (answer 20) that this note is out of date: the detail page has no Delete, and Delete is in the "Edit Library Part" window. The expected results follow the PRD.

The design's own words:

  • “Clicking a row opens the entry, where it can be edited and deleted (S11-R3). New entries come only from a part number in use (S11-R6).”
